irp.title: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan Refresh (load-forecast update to the 2024 PSO IRP; no new preferred portfolio)
irp.docket: Refresh ordered in OCC PUD Case 2025-000064 (report also cites the RFP-approval case as 2024-000064; approval Order No. 757495, May 11, 2026). Underlying full IRP: 2024 PSO IRP filed 2024-10-01.
irp.next_due: Full traditional IRP in 2027 (per refresh report)

load.energy_growth_note: Gross summer peak (before EE/DR). Annual load rises from 23,957 GWh (2027) to 76,640 GWh (2036), roughly 3.2x. The 2036 peak is 6,456 MW (+146%) above the 2024 IRP forecast of 4,413 MW. PSO says nearly all of the increase comes from new large-load customers; load from existing customers is roughly flat. Growth rate is computed from the refresh's Table 2.
load.large_load_notes: New customers over 75 MW: about 3,100 MW with signed Contracts for Electric Service plus about 3,400 MW with signed Letters of Agreement, all in the forecast without risk adjustment. The data-processing sub-sector (data centers and crypto) is modeled separately, but the refresh gives no separate data-center MW and names no customers. Trade press (not the IRP): Google confirmed in Aug 2026 that it is the end user of 'Project Clydesdale', a 506-acre data center campus built by Beale Infrastructure in unincorporated Tulsa County near Owasso and Cherokee Industrial Park, powered by PSO with a new on-site substation. Google's Muskogee and Stillwater campuses are served by OG&E, not PSO.

generation_adds.note: Northeastern Units 5 & 6, two GE F-class CTs at PSO's Northeastern site (Rogers County, OK). Approved by OCC in May 2026 and studied under SPP's ERAS fast-track process.
Green Country (existing CC) listed as owned capacity from 2026. It appears as 795 MW 'New CC' in the 2024 IRP preferred plan for 2025/26. This is an acquisition, not new construction.
Northeastern 3 converted from coal to gas-only; it stopped burning coal on 2025-12-31.
Wind PPAs approved May 2026: Weatherford 147 MW (2026), Caddo 80 MW (2027), King Plains 248 MW (2028). MW are 'SPP installed capacity' from refresh Table 6.
Six-hour BESS approved May 2026: Northeastern 1&2 100 MW, Dover 74 MW, Rock Falls 50 MW. The full 2023-RFP package, including NE 5&6, is 1,299 MW nameplate and about 923 MW summer accredited.

OPEN NEED: the refresh projects a summer accredited-capacity deficit of 99 MW in 2027, growing to 7,145 MW by 2036 (winter deficit 7,425 MW by 2035/36). It has no preferred plan; resource types will come from the 2026 All-Source RFP and the 2027 IRP.

retirements.plant: Northeastern 3 (coal operation ended; unit continues on gas)
Expiring PPAs/CPAs (e.g., Oneta 260 MW 2031, Kiamichi 150 MW 2032, several wind PPAs)

headline: PSO's August 2026 refresh more than doubles its outlook: summer peak goes from about 4.5 GW in 2026 to about 10.9 GW in 2036, almost all from large-load contracts, leaving a capacity gap of about 7 GW. A 4 GW all-source RFP is under way and a full IRP follows in 2027.

irp.title: NIPSCO 2024 Integrated Resource Plan (2026 IRP in progress)
irp.docket: IURC IRP No. 46172 (as cited in Clean Grid Alliance comments); related GenCo data-center causes: 46183 (GenCo), 46322 (Amazon), 46362 (GenCo generation), 46393 (Alphabet)
irp.next_due: 2026 IRP under way: stakeholder meeting #1 held 2026-09-23 and #2 set for 2026-10-20; filing date not confirmed (Indiana requires an IRP at least every 3 years)

load.energy_growth_note: 2024 IRP Reference Case: about 2,300 MW 'flat load' peak plus 600 MW of data-center load in 2028, 1,600 MW in 2030 and 2,600 MW by 2035. Data centers could add 21,810-72,140 GWh/yr by 2035. Emerging-load sensitivity reaches 11,100 MW peak in 2035. The IRP uses 2028 as the base year, so no 2024 actual is given here. 2026 IRP materials put NIPSCO native (non-data-center) peak at about 1,767 MW and 2,170 MW in 2027 (two seasonal charts; season labels not captured) and say signed data-center contract peaks with reserve margin are just over 3,100 MW. Growth rate is computed.
load.large_load_notes: The 2024 IRP assumed 2-3 hyperscaler projects (2,600 MW by 2035), out of six active projects (up to 8,600 MW). Since the IRP, NiSource created NIPSCO Generation LLC (GenCo; IURC approved Sept 2025) to serve data centers under special contracts. (1) Amazon Data Services: up to 2,400 MW by end-2032, service from 2027-01-01, 15-year contract approved 2026-06-17 (Cause 46322). Sites are studied at Hobart (Lake County) and Schahfer (Jasper County); Amazon has a one-time option to cut 1,200 MW by 2029-03-31. (2) Alphabet subsidiary: data center in Michigan City (LaPorte County), service from summer 2026 (Cause 46393; MW not public).

generation_adds.note: GenCo: two 1,300 MW CCGTs at the Schahfer site (Jasper County), under construction, dedicated to Amazon. This exceeds the 2024 IRP data-center path (1,285 MW CCGT plus 420 MW peaking by 2029).
GenCo Mitchell BESS (dedicated to Amazon), plus pool assets: Mitchell 100 MW, Tipton 167 MW (BTA), Nebo 75 MW (PPA), and about 500 MW of contracted generation (NiSource investor deck, Sept 2026).
NIPSCO gas peaker at Schahfer (Jasper County), pre-construction per the Sept 2026 IRP deck. Replaces Schahfer 16A/B.
2024 IRP native-load path: 900-1,150 MW of storage tied to MISO DLOL accreditation, plus 150-350 MW short-term thermal PPAs and 440 MW DSM. The 2026 IRP is reconsidering the storage size.
2024 IRP mid-term: 150-650 MW wind plus 125 MW storage. Long-term: a further 200-900 MW wind. Upper bound shown.
2024 IRP, only if data-center load is contracted.
Previously IURC-approved renewables (~1,700 MW wind/solar/solar+storage, e.g., Carpenter Wind 195 MW in Jasper County and Appleseed Solar 200 MW in Cass County, both 2025).

rfp_or_procurement: The 2024 IRP followed an all-source RFP (RFP 1 and 2), and NIPSCO said it will likely run more RFPs if hyperscaler opportunities materialize. For the 2026 IRP it issued a 2026 RFI for technology costs, including RFI 1 for dispatchable resources (2028-2032). GenCo procures capacity for data-center contracts and says the 2026 IRP will 'directly inform the amount of capacity GenCo can procure'.
headline: The 2024 IRP planned for 2,600 MW of hyperscaler load by 2035 (doubling NIPSCO's peak). Contracts have already passed that: Amazon up to 2.4 GW plus Alphabet in Michigan City, over 3,100 MW with reserves. Those loads are served by about 3 GW of new GenCo gas and batteries at Schahfer and Mitchell, while NIPSCO retires its last coal in 2028.

irp.title: 2024 Duke Energy Indiana Integrated Resource Plan
irp.docket: IURC IRP No. 46155 (as cited in Clean Grid Alliance comments); Cayuga CC CPCN Cause 46193 (approved 2025-10-29)
irp.next_due: Not announced; Indiana requires at least every 3 years, so about late 2027

load.energy_growth_note: Base winter peak (Duke plans for winter in MISO); 2030 is 5,650 MW. The IRP states summer peak CAGR of 0.39% and winter 0.85% for 2025-2044. Energy CAGR 2025-2044 is 0.55% (low), 1.02% (base) and 1.67% (high), per Table D-18 as read. Historical peak was about 6,000 MW (2023). High-case winter peak is 6,584 MW in 2030 and 7,767 MW in 2044.
load.large_load_notes: Base forecast includes about 300 MW of large economic-development projects (≥20 MW) by 2030, at about 60% weighting of announced projects. Data centers appear only in the high case (+500 MW, about 100 MW/yr from 2027). No customers are named in the excerpts read. The IRP predates Duke's 2026 data-center surge: Duke Energy (corporate, Q2 2026) reports 7.8 GW of signed data-center ESAs company-wide and 'potential for $5-10 billion of additional capital to serve large loads in Indiana and Florida', without giving Indiana-specific MW.

generation_adds.note: Cayuga Energy Complex, two 1x1 CCs (Vermillion County) replacing Cayuga coal and adding about 470 MW net. CPCN approved 2025-10-29, about $3.3B, ground broken 2026-05-14. The IRP listed 719 MW each; the CPCN rates them about 738 MW winter each.
Planned Gibson 2x1 CC (Gibson County), replacing Gibson 3 & 4. CPCN was to be filed 2025-2026; status not confirmed.
Includes Speedway Solar PPA 199 MW (2025) plus about 300 MW via RFP.
Procured through RFP.
Gibson 1 & 2 co-fire 50% natural gas (blend), plus Edwardsport IGCC conversion to 100% gas. Conversions, not new builds.
EE and demand response programs (more than 300 MW). Blend 2 adds over 1,100 MW of winter firm capacity net of retirements by 2032.

Duke's 2026 data-center pipeline is not in this IRP.

irp.title: Hoosier Energy 2023 Integrated Resource Plan
irp.regulator: Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC); IRP filed under 170 IAC 4-7. The IURC does not regulate Hoosier's rates.
irp.docket: No cause number shown on the filing; IURC Director's draft report issued 2025-04-28
irp.next_due: unknown (Indiana rule requires at least every 3 years)

load.energy_growth_note: Base-normal winter generation peak (winter-peaking system); 2040 is 1,728 MW. Load forecast is from the July 2022 RUS Power Requirements Study (2020-2040): energy CAGR 1.01% (front-loaded, 3.0%/yr 2020-2025, then about 0.3-0.5%/yr). Extreme-weather winter peak is 1,960 MW in 2040. All-time system peak is 1,828 MW (as stated in the May 2026 IURC forum deck). Growth rate is computed.
load.large_load_notes: The IRP has no data-center load. Hoosier's May 2026 IURC Summer Reliability Forum deck shows large-load interest across member systems rising from 594 MW (2020) to 6,761 MW (2023), 17,532 MW (2024) and 20,930 MW (2025): 'all projects received in calendar year with at least one site in Hoosier territory', counted as inquiries, not contracts. A Large Load/Data Center Service Policy (50 MW+) requires the customer to cover all costs to serve plus a margin. Members are 17 distribution co-ops in central/southern Indiana and southeastern Illinois.

generation_adds.note: Palisades nuclear PPA (Michigan restart). The IURC Director flagged restart uncertainty.

50% share of the 720 MW St. Joseph Energy Center CC (New Carlisle, St. Joseph County), bought jointly with Wabash Valley Power Alliance, closed 2025-03-13. Hoosier said its IRP showed gas need at end of decade. MW is computed as 50% of 720 MW.
Lincoln Land CC capacity-only PPA (Sangamon County, IL); the IRP calls it tentative. Also an Invenergy Nelson capacity PPA, 157 MW, 2026.
Generic new gas CTs in the preferred plan. Also a new gas CC of 325 MW in 2036 and new RICE of 216 MW in 2040.
Clenera Rustic Hills Solar PPA 100 MW (2026) and new solar 75 MW (2033). Board also approved a 150 MW solar resource for planning year 2026-27.
New wind 100 MW (2040) plus 50 MW (2041).

irp.title: Great River Energy 2026-2040 Integrated Resource Plan
irp.docket: MPUC IRP docket 26-145 (pending); GRE's utility prefix, likely ET2, not verified
irp.next_due: unknown (MN IRPs are generally filed every 2-3 years per Commission order)

load.energy_growth_note: Base Case (Legacy + 400 MW of large load), per Table 4. 2040 peak is 2,413 MW (2.0% CAGR 2026-2040). The step-up arrives in 2029 (1,881 MW in 2028 to 2,294 MW in 2029). Energy goes from 9,766 GWh (2026) to 13,673 GWh (2029) to 14,479 GWh (2040), a 2.85% CAGR. Legacy load without large loads grows only 0.59%/yr in peak and 0.70%/yr in energy. The High Case (+2,700 MW) reaches 4,690 MW in 2036 and 4,839 MW in 2040.
load.large_load_notes: The 400 MW Base Case large load is 'primarily driven by emerging data center development in GRE member service territory'. Medium Case is 900 MW and High Case 2,700 MW. No customers or locations are named. GRE commits to serve a portion and requires large customers to bring and fund additional resources. Large-load requests start through the member co-op (26 members, e.g., Dakota Electric in Farmington, Connexus, Stearns). GRE also runs a data-center site certification program.

generation_adds.note: Planned wind PPAs: Dodge County 228 MW (2027, Dodge County MN), Big Bend 300 MW (2028, near Mountain Lake MN), New Salem 426 MW (2029, ND), Three Waters 151 MW (2030, southern MN).

280 MW (2031) plus 140 MW (2032) of new gas CTs with fuel-oil backup. Sites under evaluation, 'in or near member-owner territory or existing power supply resource locations'.
Form Energy 100-hour iron-air storage pilot at Cambridge Station.
